hero.subtitle: A collision on I-80, the Richmond Parkway, or Barrett Avenue can leave you sorting out injuries, repairs, and insurance calls all at once. Our team helps Richmond residents with car accident claims at no upfront cost.

about.title: Richmond Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Richmond sits where I-80 and I-580 meet, and the Richmond Parkway ties the two together across the north side of the city. Barrett Avenue carries much of the local traffic in between. In 2025, the most recent final reporting year, Contra Costa County records list 453 injury collisions inside Richmond, with 618 people hurt and 8 lives lost. The counts tend to rise on Thursday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m., when the commute home is at its heaviest. If one of those collisions involved you, the next few weeks matter. Medical bills arrive before the insurance company decides anything, and the other driver's adjuster may call quickly asking for a recorded statement. You are not required to give one. We handle car accident claims on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery. Your consultation costs nothing, and you decide whether to move forward.

items.title: The clock is shorter than people think
items.desc: California gives most car accident victims two years to file, but a claim involving a city, county, or state vehicle or roadway can require notice within six months. We can tell you which deadline applies to your crash.

items.title: Partial fault does not end your claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you were partly responsible for a collision on the Parkway or I-580, you may still recover the portion that was not your fault. Adjusters know this, and they may try to shift more blame onto you than the facts support.

items.title: No fee unless there is a recovery
items.desc: We work on contingency, and California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and lost quality of life in an ordinary car accident case. You can get a full picture of your claim before paying anything.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company keeps calling me. Do I have to give them a recorded statement?
items.answer: No. You are not obligated to give a recorded statement to another driver's insurer, and doing so before you understand your injuries can hurt your claim later. It is reasonable to say you will respond once you have spoken with an attorney. Your own insurer is a different matter, since your policy may require cooperation.

items.question: I was hit near the I-80 and Richmond Parkway interchange and I think a road condition played a part. Is that handled differently?
items.answer: It can be. When a state or local agency may share responsibility, California requires a government claim to be filed first, often within six months of the crash, which is much sooner than the usual two-year limit. Photos of the scene, the exact location, and the time of day become especially important. We can review whether a public entity is involved and what deadline applies.

items.question: What should I save after a car accident in Richmond?
items.answer: Keep everything: photos of the vehicles and the intersection, the police report number, names of witnesses, medical records, and receipts for anything you paid out of pocket. Do not repair or dispose of your car until the damage has been documented. Write down what you remember while it is fresh, including the weather and traffic at the time.
